rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so we have zero information about which modalities, encoders, profile settings, or fusion strategies are effective. The most fundamental uncertainty is whether the RNA signal alone (with the simplest possible encoder) carries useful discriminative information at all. 2) What this tests: config_001 (RNA-only, single profile, PCA n2000) is the absolute minimal baseline—no learned encoder, no multi-profile aggregation, no image modality, no fusion. It establishes the performance floor for the RNA modality and confirms the pipeline works end-to-end. 3) Why it is the best use of the first experiment: It is the fastest to run (PCA requires no training), it isolates a single modality with the simplest representation, and it provides a concrete reference number against which every subsequent design choice (better RNA encoders, multi-profile aggregation, image modality, multimodal fusion) can be measured. Without this floor, we cannot tell whether added complexity is actually helping or merely adding noise. Starting here respects the principle of not assuming complex models outperform simple ones and reduces the greatest initial uncertainty with the least risk of confounding.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), we have essentially no information about whether the image modality carries useful signal. The most consequential fork in this search space is whether image features are informative at all, because it determines whether the ~36 multimodal configurations are worth exploring. Config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cleanest test of this question: it matches the baseline on profile_setting (singleprofile) and isolates the modality/representation axis. If image_only performs comparably to or better than the RNA baseline, it justifies investing subsequent experiments in multimodal fusion. If it performs substantially worse, it signals that RNA is the dominant modality and we should focus on RNA encoder and profile-setting variations instead. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the largest design decision before committing budget to more complex multimodal or multiprofile configurations.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved 0.485 accuracy, while config_010 (image_only, resnet50) was much weaker at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. However, we have no information on whether multiprofile + aggregation improves upon singleprofile for RNA. Question: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) directly extends the best-performing config by adding multiprofile with simple average-pool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile aggregation on the RNA modality. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a minimal, single-decision change from the current best (profile setting + its required aggregation), so the result cleanly tells us whether multiprofile is worth pursuing across all RNA encoders and fusion strategies. If it helps, it validates a large branch of the search space; if it does not, we can focus budget on encoder and fusion choices within singleprofile. This reduces the most impactful architectural uncertainty before investing in more complex multimodal or learned-encoder experiments.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc vs config_001 (singleprofile) at 0.485, showing a strong +10.6% gain from multiprofile aggregation. However, we only know avgpool works; we don't know whether a learned aggregation (transformer) captures inter-profile interactions that simple averaging misses. Question: config_003 changes only the aggregation method (avgpool → transformer) while holding model setting, profile setting, and RNA encoder identical to config_002, giving a clean one-variable comparison. Why best next: (1) it directly exploits the strongest signal in the history (multiprofile benefit), (2) it isolates a single design axis so the result unambiguously attributes any change to aggregation, (3) the answer will inform the aggregation choice for all subsequent multiprofile and multimodal experiments, reducing uncertainty across a large portion of the remaining search space, and (4) it avoids confounding by not simultaneously changing encoder, modality, or fusion.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the clear leader at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool is the best RNA setup found so far, and that RNA dominates image (0.59 vs 0.21). The one major untested design axis within this best setup is the RNA encoder: all four completed experiments used pca_n2000. Question: Does a learned, biologically-informed encoder (scvi_n200) improve over PCA in the same multiprofile+avgpool setting? This is a clean single-variable swap relative to config_002, isolating the encoder effect. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly tests whether the representation layer can push performance above 0.591, which is the most consequential unknown before committing budget to multimodal or other encoder variants. (2) If scvi_n200 (only 200 dims) matches or beats PCA_n2000, that strongly signals learned encoders are worth pursuing; if it falls well short, PCA is likely sufficient and budget is better spent elsewhere. (3) It avoids the confound of simultaneously changing profile setting, aggregation, or modality, making the result interpretable. (4) It is more informative than testing multimodal now, given the very weak image signal (0.21), which makes the expected multimodal gain small and the encoder question more decisive for the overall strategy.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is the current best at 0.650 acc. We know avgpool beat transformer by ~7% with pca_n2000 (0.591 vs 0.519), but it is unclear whether this aggregation preference holds with the stronger scvi_n200 encoder. Question: config_006 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping scvi_n200 + multiprofile, directly isolating the aggregation effect under the best-known encoder. Why this is the best next step: it is a clean one-variable comparison against our current best, will definitively resolve whether transformer aggregation is ever useful in this pipeline, and the answer constrains all subsequent multimodal experiments (configs 032/033, 038/039, 044/045, 050/051 all hinge on this choice). If transformer is again worse, we can eliminate it and focus remaining budget on encoder (scgpt) and modality (multimodal) questions with confidence.

Evidence: scvi_n200 with multiprofile+avgpool (config_005, acc=0.650) is the current best RNA-only configuration, and multiprofile+aggregation is clearly beneficial over singleprofile. However, we have not yet tested the scgpt encoder, which is a fundamentally different RNA representation (foundation-model pretrained vs. variational autoencoder). Question: config_008 (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) is a controlled comparison to config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) — only the RNA encoder changes, isolating its effect. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly resolves whether the top RNA encoder is scvi_n200 or scgpt, which is the single most consequential remaining design choice in the RNA pipeline before investing in multimodal fusion experiments. (2) The result will determine which encoder to pair with image modalities in subsequent multimodal trials, avoiding wasted budget on a suboptimal encoder. (3) It is a clean one-variable comparison, maximizing information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: RNA-only models dominate (best: scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer at 0.653), while image-only with resnet50 is very weak (0.208). Uncertainty: We do not yet know whether the poor image performance is due to a weak encoder (resnet50) or whether image is fundamentally uninformative for this task. This experiment (imagenet_vit_l, singleprofile) isolates the image encoder quality by changing only the encoder relative to config_010. If imagenet_vit_l substantially improves over 0.208, image has complementary signal worth exploring in multimodal fusion; if it remains weak, we can confidently deprioritize all image/multimodal configurations and focus remaining budget on RNA-only optimization. This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice because it gates the entire multimodal branch of the search space.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder (0.650-0.653 with multiprofile), and multiprofile+avgpool outperformed singleprofile for pca_n2000 (0.591 vs 0.485). However, we have not yet tested scvi_n200 with singleprofile, leaving open whether the multiprofile benefit is encoder-specific or universal. Question: config_004 (scvi_n200, singleprofile) directly isolates the profile-setting effect for the top encoder by providing a clean single-variable comparison against config_005 (same encoder, multiprofile, avgpool). Why this is the best next step: Before investing budget in multimodal configurations (which change modality, profile, and fusion simultaneously), we need to know whether multiprofile is essential for scvi_n200 or whether a simpler single-profile pipeline already captures most of the gain. If singleprofile scvi_n200 is already near 0.65, we can simplify the design and focus multimodal experiments on the more impactful question of fusion; if it drops substantially, we confirm multiprofile is a critical component that must be preserved in any multimodal extension. This single-variable experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about a core design axis with minimal confounding.

Evidence: RNA-only models (0.48–0.65) vastly outperform image-only models (0.21–0.23), and the best RNA configuration is scvi_n200 + multiprofile (avgpool: 0.650, transformer: 0.653). The critical unresolved question is whether adding the image modality provides any complementary signal on top of the already-strong RNA representation, or whether it introduces noise. This experiment (config_030: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) directly extends the best RNA-only setup (config_005) by adding resnet50 image features with simple concat fusion, isolating the effect of the image modality while keeping all other design choices at their best-evidenced settings. If it matches config_005 (~0.65), image adds no value and we should focus remaining budget on RNA-side refinements; if it substantially exceeds 0.65, multimodal fusion is worth further exploration. Using the simpler resnet50 and concat fusion minimizes confounds and makes the comparison clean. This is the highest-information next step because it resolves the single largest remaining uncertainty—whether the image channel is worth incorporating at all—before committing budget to more complex multimodal variants.
